title: Part 107 Practice Questions: What Good Prep Looks Like
sub_heading: ACS alignment, spaced practice, and unit vs course exams—plus red flags when comparing prep products.
body_html:
Draft — review before import.

In short: Good Part 107 prep is not a single 60-question dump. It is domain-aligned practice spread across units, with exams that mimic cumulative knowledge—not trivia isolated from the material you just studied.

ACS alignment

Questions should trace to FAA Airman Certification Standards knowledge areas. Random fact lists without section context weakly predict test readiness.

Quantity vs quality

Large banks help only if paired with structured review. 600+ tagged items matter when students encounter them after relevant sections—not all in one sitting.

Unit exams vs full practice exams

Unit exams validate section mastery; full-course practice simulates breadth before scheduling the testing center.

Red flags in weak prep

  • Guaranteed pass claims
  • Outdated airspace charts with no update policy
  • No connection between lesson order and quiz order

Drone Edge approach

Structured course with section practice, unit exams, and course-level practice. Teachers evaluating depth for a class can review the public preview.
